section_summary.extract_value: This section reports psychometric evaluation of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) for Brazilian adolescents, including CFA fit indices (e.g., RMSEA = .038 for the original model and .022 after re-specification), item analysis (item 12 considered for deletion), internal consistency (α = .804 overall; .752 boys; .851 girls), and validity analyses. Convergent validity showed a negative correlation between BAS and BMI for the overall sample (r = -0.230) and for females (r = -0.338); criterion analyses (ANOVA, N = 343) indicated normal-weight participants had higher BAS scores than obese participants.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports psychometric evaluation of the original unidimensional Body Appreciation Scale (BAS): fit indices were acceptable and Item 12 showed very low loading but removing it did not substantially improve fit. Concurrent validity showed a negative correlation between BAS and BMI for the total sample (r = -0.230) and especially females (r = -0.338); males showed a small non-significant negative correlation (r = -0.105). Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) was adequate for the total sample and by sex.
